newsitem.title: UK: Russia drifts in slow emerging debt market.
newsitem.headline: Russia drifts in slow emerging debt market.

text.p: The emerging debt market was largely at a standstill in early Monday trading, with few incentives to take fresh positions ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday on November 8, traders said.
Russian debt was a bit wobbly after last week's profit-taking.
"It's still positive. There's no news, so it's drifting but looking ahead it seems good," one trader said.
Vnesh dollar debt RUVNUSLNS=RR was bid 1/8 of a point lower at 78-3/8 cents in the dollar. MinFins also slipped in early trading but later recovered.

Another trader said that with the Eurobond now issued and President Boris Yeltsin apparently continuing his recovery from heart surgery, some may be looking at Belarus's dispute with Russia as a reason to sell.
"It is something that is happening close by, like Chechnya. People are talking about it and some might use it as an excuse to sell," he said.

A political compromise Yeltsin had pushed for between the head of state and parliament in neighbouring Belarus lay in ruins after President Alexander Lukashenko went ahead with Sunday's referendum to greatly increase his powers.
Lukashenko claimed a crushing victory in the vote.
Bulgaria was holding steady, as measures by the central bank helped prop up the tumbling lev, but traders said the country's Bradys remained very volatile, with default a lingering risk.
Elsewhere, Latin American debt barely traded though Brazil C bonds were a touch stronger.
